correctness.rationale: Independently generated all perfect matchings of each two-antipodal-chord deleted M_{2n} with n=3,4,5 by recursive pairing of the smallest unmatched vertex, then all downward-closed faces. From independent lexicographic free-face searches, exact elementary collapses count 3,12,8,64,55, respectively, leaving graphs (v,e,c)=(7,6,1),(10,8,2),(8,6,2),(13,14,1),(13,12,1). Thus terminal ranks e-v+c are 0,0,0,2,0 with two components at n=4, precisely *, S0, S0, S1 vee S1, *. Entire small domain and both chord distances are exhausted. The original certificate was also inspected, but the independent reduction does not rely on its saved pairs.
residual_risks: No claim for n>=6, equivariant topology or deletion inclusion maps.

originality.rationale: Read the 19-page original Agarwal–Basak preprint through authorized paper extraction, including the complete intact Möbius/circular ladder main theorem and relevant Section 5 lemmas. It treats original undeleted ladders, not two-chord defects and their separation-dependent homotopy. Also read the published one-antipodal-rung deletion theorem; its contractibility for even n does not entail deleting a second rung, particularly the d=1 vs d=2 difference at n=5. Relevant Resultary rim-edge deletion changes a different edge class. Best-of-knowledge novel exact first separation-sensitive case.
residual_risks: A published/unindexed general defect theorem could cover the first two deletions; no historical priority guarantee.

value.rationale: Two identical antipodal-edge deletions with different relative separations yield drastically different topology at the smallest possible ladder size: the natural 10-vertex instance changes from a wedge of two circles to contractible. The exact exhaustive finite homotopy threshold and explicit collapses are useful defect-sensitivity data, despite not giving a general n recursion.
residual_risks: Does not classify n>=6 or all edge-deletion patterns.

limitations: Original paper only intact ladders; broad prior classification under different terminology still possible.
